Alex — great questions, thanks. Quick answers inline and proposed next steps below.

- Scope of logs: Hosted defaults to capturing request metadata and token-level telemetry; bodies are not persisted in full by default unless a customer enables request/response logging. When enabled, bodies can be stored in a configurable manner: full (not recommended), truncated (first NKB), or redacted according to masking rules.

- Headers: header logging is configurable. Authorization/Cookie headers are excluded by default. We can apply allowlists/denylists per-header. We recommend no Authorization or Cookie in logs.

- Trace IDs: we support hashing/pepper for trace IDs so stored values are pseudo-identifiers that cannot be trivially tied back to raw trace IDs. Deterministic hashing (same input -> same output) is available if you need consistent pseudonyms for analytics; rotateable keyed-hash is available for stronger unlinkability.

- Masking vs redaction: both options supported. Deterministic pseudonymization (consistent masks) is supported for fields like user_id or account_number. For fields like full_name or email we recommend one-way hashing or full redaction depending on use. We can provide sample configs.

- Retention: Hosted default = 30 days for request/response logs; Dedicated and Private can support longer, customer-defined retention (365 days or more) and on-request export for audits. For hosted we can discuss an enterprise retention add-on if needed.

Attached: SOC2-whitepaper.pdf (stub) and a sample redaction snippet (included below).

Sample redaction config (example):
- fields_to_mask: [email, ssn, account_number]
- mask_strategy: deterministic_hash (sha256 + customer_salt)
- headers_denylist: [Authorization, Cookie, x-custom-secret]
- trace_id_handling: keyed_hash (rotate_key: quarterly)

Proposed next steps:
1) Security deep-dive with Rishi and Dev to walk through the config and run a short demo of masking (45 mins)
2) You send PII classes and desired retention
3) We'll produce a short statement of work for retention/residency options (if Dedicated/Private is required)
